:::{#thm-chebyshev}
#### Chebyshev's inequality: a random variable is at least $k$ standard deviations from its mean with probability at most $1/k^2$

Let $X$ be a [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable)
with [expectation](expectation.qmd#def-expectation) $\mean$
and a finite, positive [variance](variance-covariance.qmd#def-variance) $\varpar$, <!-- check-term-links: allow: finite means a real number here, not a finite set -->
and let $k$ be a positive number.
Then the [probability](probability-basics.qmd#def-probability) that $X$ is at least $k$
[standard deviations](variance-covariance.qmd#def-sd) $\sdpar$ from $\mean$
is at most $1/k^2$
[@wikipedia_chebyshevs_inequality]:

$$
\Prf{\abs{X - \mean} \ge k\sdpar} \le \frac{1}{k^2}
$$

:::

::: proof

The random variable $(X - \mean)^2$ is nonnegative,
and its expectation is $\varpar$.
Because $\abs{X - \mean} \ge k\sdpar$ exactly when $(X - \mean)^2 \ge k^2\varpar$,
@thm-markov gives

$$
\Prf{\abs{X - \mean} \ge k\sdpar}
= \Prf{(X - \mean)^2 \ge k^2\varpar}
\le \frac{\varpar}{k^2\varpar}
= \frac{1}{k^2}
$$

:::
